'''James E. Atwater''' (born September 22, 1946) is a retired North American multidisciplinary physical scientist with training in [[geophysics]], chemistry, and biological science. Atwater holds courtesy faculty appointments with the [[University of Oregon]] Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uoregon.edu/findpeople/person/personid/41430 |title=Find People &#124; University of Oregon |publisher=Uoregon.edu |date= |accessdate=2022-06-10}}</ref>  and the School of Chemical, Biological and [[Environmental engineering|Environmental Engineering]] at [[Oregon State University]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://directory.oregonstate.edu/?type=search&cn=james+atwater&surname=&mail=&telephonenumber=&osualtphonenumber=&osuofficeaddress=&osudepartment=&affiliation=any&anyphone= |title=Online Directory, Oregon State University |publisher=Directory.oregonstate.edu |date= |accessdate=2022-06-10}}</ref> On [[ResearchGate]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/James-Atwater-2 |title=James E. Atwater |website=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref> he has accumulated a score for Research Interest of 396.4 with a total of 8,689 reads and 811 citations of his [[Peer review|peer-reviewed]] publications, as of April 23, 2026. He was awarded the [[Wright Brothers Medal]]<ref>[http://www.sae.org/servlets/awardInfo?OBJECT_TYPE=awardInfo&PAGE=awardRecipients&REQUEST_FROM=&BEGIN_YEAR=2006&END_YEAR=2006&Submit=submit "List of Wright Brothers Medal recipients"], [[Society of Automotive Engineers]]. Retrieved June 2, 2008. Award citation: "Development and Testing of a Microwave Powered Solid Waste Stabilization and Water Recovery System"</ref> for his work on microwave-powered methods for [[microbial]] stabilization and water recovery from solid waste. Atwater served in the [[United States Marine Corps]] (1963–1967) prior to attending the [[University of Utah]] (1968–1975) and [[University at Albany]] (1975).

==Early life and career==
In his early career (1977–1980), Atwater concentrated on methods and instrumentation for identification and quantification of radionuclides associated with uranium exploration and recovery by [[gamma ray]] and [[alpha particle]] energy [[Gamma spectroscopy|spectrometry]]. Subsequently, (1980–1987) he applied radiometric geophysical well logging techniques to the characterization of [[sandstone]], limestone, dolomite and shale core samples.<ref>Atwater, J.E., Spectrometric Gamma Ray Logging of Core, Canadian Well Logging Society Journal 13(1), 29–39, 1984.<br />- Matiisen, A., and Atwater, J.E., "An Overview of Computer-Enhanced Analyses of Core Data", ''Journal of Canadian Petroleum Technology'' '''23'''(3), 57–62, 1984.<br />- Atwater, J.E., "Correlation of Cation Exchange Capacity with Core Spectral Gamma Ray Logs", SPWLA 27th Annual Logging Symposium, Paper QQ, pp 1–16, 1986.<br />- Codding, E.G., and Atwater, J.E., "Application of Core Hydrocarbon Logging", ''Proceedings of the 37th Annual Technical Meeting of the Petroleum Society of CIM'', Paper No. 86–37–20, pp 273–284, 1986.</ref> At this time he also refined methods for the determination of porosity and permeability of unconsolidated bitumen and heavy oil bearing sands. Later Atwater's attention turned to problems of long-term human presence in space, working on regenerable systems for water and air purification,<ref>Atwater, J.E., and Holtsnider, J.T., "Airborne Trace Organic Contaminant Removal Using Thermally Regenerable Multi-Media Layered Sorbents", ''SAE Transactions'', ''Journal of Aerospace'' 100, 1726–1733, 1991.<br />- Atwater, J.E.,  Wheeler, R.R., Jr., Olivadoti, J.T., Flanagan, D.T. and Sauer, R.L., "Regenerable Microbial Check Valve: Life Cycle Tests Results", ''SAE Transactions, Journal of Aerospace'' 101, 1098–1107, 1992.<br />- Atwater, presented at 27th International Conference on Environmental Systems, Lake Tahoe, Nevada, July 14–17, 1997.<br />- Wheeler, R.R., Jr., Atwater, J.E., Akse, J.R., Holtsnider, J.T., and Luna, B.,  "Development and Testing of a Microwave Powered Regenerable Air Purification Technology Demonstrator", ''SAE Technical Paper 2002-01-2403'', presented at 32nd International Conference on Environmental During these years Atwater and colleagues also developed novel sensors and analytical instrumentation for monitoring and control of life support systems.<ref>Atwater, J.E., Wheeler, R.R., Jr., Sauer, Liquid-Solid Fluidization in Normal and Microgravity Conditions: Experiment and Theory", ''Powder Technology'' '''148''', 80–91, 2004.<br />- Atwater, J.E., and Akse, J.R., "Cobalt – Poly(amido amine) Ag<sub>2</sub>O – Ag<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> System at Microwave Frequencies and Temperatures between 22*C and 189*C", ''Applied Physics'' A 75, 555–558, 2002.<br />- Atwater, J.E., and Wheeler, R.R., Jr., "Complex Permittivities and Dielectric Relaxation of Granular Activated Carbons at Microwave Frequencies between 0.2 and 26 GHz", ''Carbon'' '''41'''(9), 1801–1807, 2003.<br />- Atwater, J.E., and Wheeler, R.R., Jr., "Temperature Dependent Complex Permittivities of Graphitized Carbon Blacks at Microwave Frequencies Between 0.2 and 26 GHz", ''Journal of Materials Science'' '''39'''(1), 151–157, 2004.<br />- Atwater, J.E., and Wheeler, R.R., Jr., "Microwave Permittivity and Dielectric Relaxation of a High Surface Area Activated Carbon", ''Applied Physics'' A 79, 125–129, 2004.</ref> Other research includes the study of multiphase immiscible fluid flow in porous media, and the recovery of hydrogen from methane (natural gas) using magnetically stabilized fluidized bed and microwave plasma reactors.<ref>Atwater, J.E., Wheeler, R.R., Jr., Hadley, N.M., Dahl, R.W., and Carrasquillo, R.L., "Hydrogen Recovery by Methane Decomposition in a Microwave Plasma Reactor", ''SAE International Journal of Aerospace'' 1, 337–346, 2009.</ref> Though in retirement, Atwater continues his association with former colleagues, providing theoretical analysis of experimental data and preparation of materials for publication.

==Family==
Atwater is the son of the noted [[avalanche control]] pioneer and author [[Montgomery Atwater]]; the grandson of Maxwell Atwater, the first mining engineer to employ flotation hydrometallurgy in North America; and the grandson of [[Mary Meigs Atwater]], the "Dean of American Hand Weaving". Other notable family members include his great-aunt [[Cornelia Meigs]], a noted teacher historian and novelist; his great-grandfather [[Montgomery C. Meigs Jr.]], an accomplished civil engineer; and his great-great-grandfather Brigadier General [[Montgomery C. Meigs]], a military and civil engineer, Quartermaster General of the Army during the [[American Civil War]], and one of those present at the death bed of President [[Abraham Lincoln]]
